Screen candidates to the ones participants actually support

Source: R/screening.R
screen_candidates.Rd

A candidate family large enough to cover the observed data is far larger than the set any one participant is compatible with. Retaining the nu best candidates per participant and pooling them keeps the support the data speak to and makes the weight estimation tractable.

Usage

screen_candidates(loglik, nu = 200L)

Arguments

loglik

A participant-by-candidate log-likelihood matrix.

nu

Number of candidates retained per participant. Larger nu keeps more of the family at the cost of a bigger weight problem; the retained count is not usually binding, because the maximiser on a fixed support has at most one positive weight per participant.

Value

A list with the pooled candidate indices keep, the screened matrix loglik, and the number of candidates before and after.

Details

The screen uses the measurements, so the pooled support is a function of the donor data. That is a data-dependent step: it must be run on the donors only, never on a participant who will later be scored against the result, or the honesty condition fails. It also means the support is random, which the fixed-support consistency theory does not cover.

See also

fit_bank(), screen_positive()

Examples

set.seed(1)
LL <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 200), 30, 200)
s <- screen_candidates(LL, nu = 20)
c(before = s$before, after = s$after)
#> before  after 
#>    200    189
